text:
maria: quick summary — noticed a ~20-30% tail latency bump on TP + flash-attn when using small interactive batches and KV cache enabled. reproduces on 8xA100 reserved pool.

lee: saw that too on a customer run yesterday, similar traces. looks like all-gather is being triggered more frequently than before.

sri: can you paste the perf trace? is it the qkv all-gather or the scatter step?

maria: here's a short flame from nvprof + our tracer (timestamps are relative):
```
[0.00] compute: fused_attn_forward (kernel) 3.2ms
[0.01] comm: ncclAllGather (QKV) 1.9ms
[0.03] compute: kv_cache_write 0.6ms
[0.04] comm: ncclAllReduce (grad placeholder) 0.5ms
[0.05] idle/wait 2.1ms
```
notably the comms are interleaving with small compute chunks and we see a long idle between steps.

andrew: that idle looks like scheduling overhead + RTOS context switching waiting for kv cache write to finish. also curious about our batching heuristic — are small batches disabling fused kernels?

lee: i dug into kernel selector logs. for seq_len <= 64 and batch_size <= 4 we fall back to the "split-qkv" path to avoid register pressure. that increases frequency of all-gather calls (per micro-batch) instead of amortizing across larger fused ops.

maria: yes, selector picks flash-attn only when combined tokens >= 512 (approx). interactive workloads with long KV cache produce lots of short-generation steps so we keep hitting the non-fused path.

perf-bot: automated regression alert: 2026-11-02T14:12:03Z - TP fused-attn tail latency +22% vs baseline (p<0.01) in 8xA100 pool.

sri: two hypotheses: (1) kernel selector threshold too aggressive for TP layout (we should consider token-per-device metric not global tokens), (2) KV cache flush/write synchronization blocks scheduling causing comms to not overlap.

andrew: agree. small suggestion: try changing selector to prefer fused path when (tokens_per_tp_device >= 128) even if global tokens < 512. that biases toward fewer all-gathers.

lee: we also need to look at our batching heuristics. currently continuous-batcher flushes on max_wait=3ms, which for small interactive sequences triggers a flush before other in-flight requests can join. increasing to 6ms reduced all-gather count in a local sim.

maria: i ran a microbenchmark: with modified selector + batcher wait=6ms on 8xA100: tail latency drops ~18% and all-gather calls per second drop by ~35%. attaching traces (snip):
```
before: allgather/sec 1200, fused-kernel hits 22%
after:  allgather/sec 780, fused-kernel hits 56%
```

sri: great. any KV cache behavior edgecases? e.g., writes that block GPU streams?

maria: yes — our kv_cache write path currently does a host->device memcpy synchronously on the default stream for TP shards. when the shard is being updated mid-generation it serializes with the compute stream on that device. we should use an async cudaMemcpy + event-based synchronization to let comms overlap.

andrew: can we do pinned staging buffers + async copies on a dedicated stream per device? then mark event and continue. that should cut the idle time.

lee: i'll prototype async KV writes + event handshake. also will add a tokens_per_device knob to kernel selector and a small experiments matrix for batcher wait.

maria: action items:
- lee: prototype async KV writes + update mem path (ETA 2d)
- lee: add tokens_per_device threshold to selector & config toggles (ETA 1d)
- andrew: run end-to-end cluster sim with both changes and measure allgather/sec + tail latency (ETA 3d)
- sri: write a short regression test that simulates interactive tiny batches with KV caching enabled (ETA 2d)

perf-bot: note: please tag perf-bot when merging selector changes to auto-run the regression suite. :robot_face:

maria: thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review traces. @lee @andrew @sri :thumbsup:

lee: :thumbsup:
sri: +1
andrew: will do
